newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Coles says retail EBIT down 14.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Coles says retail EBIT down 14.8 pct.

text.p: Retailer Coles Myer Ltd said on Tuesday that earnings from retail operations declined 14.8 percent to A$534.6 million for the year to July 28, 1996.

Non-retail earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) fell by 57.1 percent to A$43.8 million, largely due to lower property sales and earnings, coupled with the lack of income from the company's interest in the credit card operation, ARFN, which was sold in July 1995.
Coles Myer earlier announced a 33.8 percent fall in net profit for 1995/96 to A$280.4 million.

Chief executive Peter Bartels said in a statement that a strong performance from the supermarkets and liquor businesses, representing just over 50 percent of the company's operations, and good contributions from Target discount department stores and Katies fashion chain, had been countered by disappointing results from Kmart and Myer Grace Bros department stores.
Bartels said Kmart was affected by an apparel downturn, poor Christmas trading and intense competition and discounting, together with the effects of an operational restructuring.
Bartels said Myer Grace Bros department stores recorded a 26.8 percent decline in EBIT to A$90.2 million on a sales increase of 0.9 percent to A$3.23 billion.
"The business was affected by aggressive competitor activity, particularly in apparel," Bartels said.
EBIT from Target discount deparment stores fell 2.2 percent to A$138.5 million in a tough apparel market.

"Officeworks, with 11 stores, delivered an outstanding performance with comparable stores sales up 23.7 percent," he said. "New business development costs meant an EBIT loss of A$10 million, significantly better than budget forecasts."
Property sales during 1995/96 totalled A$134.4 million, reducing property rental and management income, with some offsetting reductions in interest costs.
"A review of the future of the company's A$1.4 billion proerty portfolio is continuing and an announcement is expected prior to the end of December 1996," Bartels said.
Coles Myer's year net profit result of A$280.4 million was within an analysts' forecasts, which ranged between A$272 million and A$304 million.
